messages.text: Hi Professor Alvarez, Chris — I'd like to set up a 30-minute meeting for next week to go over my research progress. Would Wednesday 10:00-10:30 work? That slot is the only one I can make next week.

Hello — Professor Alvarez here (CSE455). A quick check on the official schedule for next week: I have Wednesday 10:00-11:00 down as Faculty senate. Could that meeting be moved or shortened on Wednesday, or is 10:00-11:00 firm? A doctoral student of mine can only meet this week's Wednesday at 10:00-10:30, so I would like to know whether the senate meeting can give way, and if so, to what time.

Ajay, Chris — noted. Ajay, Wednesday 10:00-10:30 collides with a university meeting I have that hour (Faculty senate, 10:00-11:00), so it cannot be booked as it stands. I am checking with the department office whether that meeting can move or be shortened on Wednesday; I will confirm on this thread as soon as I hear back. If it cannot move, we will have to find another slot — send me the hours you could do besides Wednesday 10:00, in case.

Good morning, Professor Alvarez. The official schedule for next week is unchanged: Faculty senate is Wednesday 10:00-11:00, and nothing on it has been cancelled, moved or shortened. I can't move or shorten other people's meetings myself — that would be for you and the senate to agree between you. What I can tell you is only what the schedule lists.

Ajay — the department confirms the official schedule is unchanged, so Wednesday 10:00-10:30 is out: I am in Faculty senate that hour and it cannot be moved or shortened. I am sorry to say that slot cannot be booked.

I do want to go over your progress. Send me the hours you could manage outside the senate hour — Wednesday 11:00-12:00 is free on my side, as is Tuesday 11:00-13:00 and Thursday 10:30-11:00. If none of those work, give me two or three windows and I will see what I can move.

Thanks for the quick reply, Professor Alvarez — and for checking with the department office.

I should be straight with you: Wednesday 10:00-10:30 really is the only slot I can do next week. Everything else is filled — lectures, lab, reading group, TA grading and my research blocks take up the rest of my working hours. So I don't have alternative hours to send, unfortunately: if the faculty senate meeting can move or be shortened, Wednesday 10:00 works; if it can't, I'd rather postpone the meeting than have you rearrange your week around me for something else.

I'll wait to hear what the office says. Thanks again. — Ajay

Understood, and thank you for checking with the office, Professor Alvarez. Then let's postpone: Tuesday 11:00-13:00 and Thursday 10:30-11:00 are inside my CSE452 lecture and lab/office hours, so I can't take those, and Wednesday 11:00-12:00 runs into my work block that hour as well.

So realistically I have no alternative windows next week. Rather than make you move things around me, could we aim for the following week, or for any half-hour that lands near Wednesday 10:00 on your side? I'll keep my Wednesday 10:00 open and let you know if anything opens up on mine. — Ajay

Ajay — thank you for being precise about your week; that saves us both time.

On my side there is no half-hour near Wednesday 10:00 to give you: I lecture 09:00-10:00, the senate hour is 10:00-11:00, and grant writing runs 11:00-12:30. So Wednesday 10:00-10:30 is closed on both sides next week, and you have nothing else free — let us postpone, as you suggest.

For the week of Monday 23 November I can hold a half-hour for your progress meeting; send me your free hour that week (Wednesday 10:00 included, if it comes free again) and I will book it as soon as the official schedule for that week is posted. And the offer stands: if you send me a written progress note on this thread meanwhile, I will read it and reply with comments so the fortnight is not idle. — Professor Alvarez

Ajay — fair enough, and sorry the week is so tight.

On my side: I'd put Wednesday 10:00-10:30 in my calendar when you first proposed it, but since the Professor is in Faculty senate that hour and the official schedule can't move, that slot can't be booked. I've taken it back out, so nothing is holding it.

Postponing seems the sane call — the following week, or the first half-hour near Wednesday 10:00 that works on both your sides. I'll keep my Wednesday morning free of anything else in case you land there, and if a slot opens near it I'll say so here.

Agreed then — let's postpone to the week of Monday 23 November. My week has the same shape as this one, so the hour that works for me is again Wednesday 10:00-10:30; please hold it once the official schedule for that week is posted, and I'll keep it clear on my side.

And yes, I'd like to take you up on the written progress note — here is a short one, and I'll add to it as the results firm up:

**Progress note, week of 16 November**
- Literature: finished the reading block on the two lines of work closest to my topic and wrote up the comparison; it clarifies where my approach differs.
- Method: the setup from last term is running end to end and I have the first results; they are encouraging but still too few to claim much.
- Next: repeat the runs with more seeds and a held-out setting, then write the first version of the results section.

If you'd rather take the half-hour next week and keep the written feedback for later, that's fine too — either way I'll have something more solid to show by then. — Ajay

Thanks, Chris — that matches what I told the Professor: nothing is booked for next week, and we're aiming for the week of Monday 23 November, Wednesday 10:00-10:30 again, to be confirmed once that week's official schedule is posted. Good to know your Wednesday morning is free; if anything shifts near it on my side I'll say so here. — Ajay

That settles it then: nothing booked for next week, and Ajay's Wednesday 10:00-10:30 is not held on my side either.

Ajay — once you know your free hour for the week of 23 November, put it here and I'll check it against my own week; if you'd rather, send the progress note first and I'll read it alongside the Professor's comments.

Chris — noted, and thank you for clearing it. Nothing is booked for next week, so no slot is held anywhere; we aim for the week of 23 November with Ajay. Your keeping Wednesday morning free is helpful — if the official schedule for that week leaves 10:00 free, that is where I would put the meeting, and I will confirm here once I have it. — Professor Alvarez

Both are already up there, Chris: my free hour for the week of 23 November is Wednesday 10:00-10:30, and the short progress note is in my previous message for the Professor to comment on. Ping me here if either needs moving. — Ajay

Hello — Chris here (graduate student, advised by Professor Alvarez). Could you tell me when the official schedule for the week of Monday 23 November is expected to be posted, and whether the Faculty senate hour (Wednesdays 10:00-11:00) is on it again that week? Ajay and Professor Alvarez are trying to fix a half-hour progress meeting that week and want to book as soon as the schedule is official. Thank you.

Good — I've read the progress note, Ajay; it's a clear picture of where the work stands.

I've written to the department office asking when the official schedule for the week of 23 November goes up, and whether the senate hour is on it again that Wednesday, so we can book Wednesday 10:00-10:30 as soon as it's official. I'll report back on this thread when they answer.

On my side: Wednesday 10:00-10:30 that week is free, so I have nothing to move.
Thanks, Chris — that's helpful. I'll keep Wednesday 10:00-10:30 clear on my side and wait for the department's word, then we can book it. — Ajay

Understood — Ajay's note is in this thread and Wednesday 10:00-10:30 of the week of 23 November is the target, on my side free as well. I'll pass on whatever the department office says about that week's schedule, and hold the slot once it's confirmed.

Hello Chris. The schedule for the week of Monday 23 November is already in effect, and it is unchanged: Faculty senate is on it, Wednesday 10:00-11:00. That is all I can tell you from the schedule — I don't arrange other people's meetings, so I can't advise on booking a slot.

One clarification, please. The official schedule I hold for next week — does it cover Monday 23 to Friday 27 November, and does it list Faculty senate on Wednesday 10:00-11:00? I want to be certain which week I am booking against. And when will the schedule for the week of Monday 30 November be posted? One student of mine can only meet on Wednesday 10:00-10:30, so I may need that later week.

Ajay — thank you for the note; it is a good one. Before the booking, one correction, because the dates matter: the week of Monday 23 November **is** the week I already hold the official schedule for, and I have just asked the office to confirm its dates. In that week Wednesday 10:00-11:00 is Faculty senate, unchanged, so Wednesday 23... Wednesday 10:00-10:30 in the week of 23 November is closed on my side too — the same clash, not a new one. If the office confirms this, our next real window is the week of Monday 30 November; I will ask for that schedule and confirm the slot here as soon as it exists.

On the note itself, three comments:

- The comparison write-up is the right place to have put your time. Now reduce it to two sentences: what the two existing lines cannot do that yours can. That becomes the gap statement in the paper.
- More seeds and a held-out setting is the correct next step. Fix the metric and the baseline budget before you launch the runs, so the extra compute buys a claim rather than a number.
- Send me the results-section draft when the runs are in; I will read it then, and we keep the half-hour for your progress meeting rather than for feedback.

Chris — no action needed from you; I will post the confirmed date here. — Professor Alvarez

Yes: the schedule I hold covers Monday 23 to Friday 27 November, and it lists Faculty senate on Wednesday 10:00-11:00. I don't have a posting date for the following week (Monday 30 November onward), so I can't say when that will be available — I only know the official schedule for the coming week.

Word back from the department office: the schedule for the week of Monday 23 November is already in effect and unchanged — Faculty senate is on it, Wednesday 10:00-11:00.

So Wednesday 10:00-10:30 that week runs into exactly the same conflict as this one, and can't be booked while the senate hour stands. Ajay, if your week has the same shape as this week's, we're in the same position as before — and the office says it doesn't move faculty meetings.

Professor Alvarez — you said you'd book once that week's schedule was posted; it is up now, and it keeps your senate hour. If Wednesday 10:00-10:30 is out, could you name the half-hours you can hold that week and Ajay and I will see which of them he can reach? I have Wednesday morning free, and my other blocks that week are fixed.

Thank you, Professor Alvarez — the comments are clear and I'll work to them: two sentences on what the existing lines can't do that mine can, as the gap statement; and metric and baseline budget fixed before the runs start. I'll send the results-section draft once the runs are in, and keep the half-hour for the meeting itself.

On the booking: one thing to keep straight, since the dates matter. Earlier you said the schedule for the week of 23 November was not posted yet and that you would hold a half-hour there; now it sounds as if that week is already in hand, with the senate hour on it again on Wednesday. If it is, then yes — that week is closed and the next real window is the week of Monday 30 November, where my free hour is again Wednesday 10:00-10:30. Please book that as soon as that week's schedule exists. If the week of 23 November does turn out to have Wednesday 10:00 free, that works for me too and I'd take it. — Ajay

Thank you — that is exactly what I needed to know. So the week of 23-27 November carries Faculty senate on Wednesday 10:00-11:00, and the following week's schedule is not yet posted. Please let me know when the schedule from 30 November onward is available; I have a student whose only free hour is Wednesday 10:00-10:30, so I will want to book against that week. — Professor Alvarez

Thanks for chasing it, Chris.

So that's settled: the week of 23 November keeps the senate hour, and Wednesday 10:00-10:30 there is closed for the same reason as this week. To be explicit so nobody has to guess at my side: my week has the same shape as this one — CSE444 Monday and Wednesday mornings, CSE452 lectures, lab and office hours Tuesday and Thursday, reading group Tuesday afternoon, TA grading Wednesday afternoon, research blocks filling the rest — so the only half-hour I can reach, in either week, is Wednesday 10:00-10:30. There is no other hour for me to name.

Professor Alvarez: then the next real window is the week of Monday 30 November, where my hour is again Wednesday 10:00-10:30. Please book it once that week's schedule is up, and I'll keep that half-hour clear. Meanwhile I'm getting on with the runs and the gap statement, and the results-section draft will reach you when they're in. — Ajay

That means 23 November is closed on your side as well, exactly as you say, and next week is off.

So the next real window is the week of Monday 30 November. I'll ask the office when that week's schedule is posted; if it keeps your senate hour, Ajay's Wednesday 10:00-10:30 will clash again there too, and we'd be wise to have a fallback half-hour agreed in advance. I'll report what the office says here.

Thank you, that's exactly what I needed. One more: when is the official schedule for the week of Monday 30 November posted — is it in effect yet? Professor Alvarez plans to book Ajay's progress meeting in that week, and I'd like to know whether the senate hour (Wednesday 10:00-11:00) is on it, so nobody books into it. I understand you don't arrange meetings; I'm only asking about the schedule.
